name: Super Furry Animals
label: Creation Records
lede: Five Welshmen who started out playing techno with a Hollywood actor on vocals, put a drug smuggler on their first album cover, drove a blue tank to festivals, and made the biggest-selling Welsh-language album there is.

eras.title: Techno, Welsh and a very long word
eras.text: Gruff Rhys had already fronted Ffa Coffi Pawb, one of the leading bands of the Welsh-language scene. His new band began as a techno act in Cardiff, sang in Welsh, and put out its first record on the Welsh indie Ankst.

years.src: Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals · Wikipedia: Gruff Rhys
years.h: Rhys Ifans sings for a Cardiff techno band
years.p: Rhys and drummer [[Dafydd Ieuan|0af7c149-7887-4bf7-813c-7fd9f091661e]] start the band with [[Huw Bunford|d9dab2ca-5f55-48cc-8bd9-24142693dc66]] and [[Guto Pryce|abed13cb-594b-4e92-8f46-1ccd0ea9014c]], with the actor [[Rhys Ifans|eb7900ee-95a2-43fc-8ff5-963aa5709558]] on vocals. The name comes off T-shirts Rhys's sister made for the Acid Casuals collective.

years.h: Cian Ciaran joins from Wwzz, and Ankst signs the five
years.p: Gruff's brother [[Cian Ciaran|7adbe63b-2576-41da-ab03-05373a67e632]] brings keyboards and electronics from his electronic outfit Wwzz. The five-piece signs to the Welsh label Ankst.

years.h: Guinness logs the longest EP title ever
years.p: The debut EP takes the name of the Anglesey village and adds a space flight. Every song is in Welsh; so is the Moog Droog EP that October, bar "God! Show Me Magic."

years.h: Alan McGee asks Gruff Rhys to try singing in English
years.p: McGee of Creation Records caught the band at the Camden Monarch in London, and signed them. Rhys's answer to the English note is the story McGee tells on himself.
years.xp: McGee's version: "The sound through the PA was that bad I thought Gruff Rhys was singing in Welsh. I told him afterwards it would help sales if he'd sing in English, and he said, 'I was!'"

eras.title: A smuggler, a tank and 50-odd swears
eras.text: Creation's new Welsh signing made a debut album in a studio with jacuzzis, hung it on Howard Marks, toured festivals with giant bears, and put out a single that radio couldn't touch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals · Wikipedia: Fuzzy Logic
years.h: "Hometown Unicorn" is NME's Single of the Week
years.p: The first single on Creation stalls at No. 47. "God! Show Me Magic" gets to No. 33 in April.

years.h: Howard Marks, in many disguises, is the face of Fuzzy Logic
years.p: The cover is a photomontage of the Welsh drug smuggler, who came to Rockfield Studios at the band's invitation. One song is called "Hangin' with Howard Marks."
years.xp:
Why Rockfield? "We wanted to record there because they had jacuzzis and you got three meals a day." Gorwel Owen co-produced, and the album reached No. 23.

NME's Simon Williams said debut albums "rarely come as multi-layered, as lovingly-manipulated as this."

years.cap: The band beside the SFA tank at the National Eisteddfod, 1996
years.h: A blue tank with SFA on the side rolls into the festivals
years.p: Summer shows come with 40-foot inflatable bears and a tank painted blue with the band's initials.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Man Don't Give a Fuck · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: Donald Fagen clears the Steely Dan sample, for 95 percent
years.p: Built on "Show Biz Kids," it swears more than 50 times, so it gets almost no airplay. It still reaches No. 22, and Rhys took the deal because he expected no airplay anyway.
years.xp:
It was meant as a B-side to "If You Don't Want Me to Destroy You" until the sample was cleared. Fagen had first refused, unhappy with how prominent the sample was.

It became the band's set-closer, with Cian Ciaran stretching the end out to 10 or 20 minutes. A 23-minute live take from the Hammersmith Apollo came out in 2004, with around 100 uses of the word.
play: The Man Don't Give a Fuck
The Man Don't Give a Fuck

years.src: Wikipedia: Radiator · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: Creation releases Radiator four days after Be Here Now
years.p: Gorwel Owen's Atari computers and vintage synths, and the first of Pete Fowler's paintings for the band's sleeves. It reaches No. 8.
years.xp: Rhys said Owen's setup made it "musically ... much more adventurous" than the debut. The label's own [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]] record landed the same week. NME later put Radiator at No. 92 of its 500 greatest albums.

eras.title: Best new band, three years late
eras.text: The singles got bigger, the records got stranger, and when Creation came apart the band made the album it wanted in its own language for £6,000.

years.h: "Smokin'" gets the band onto Top of the Pops
years.p: From the Ice Hockey Hair EP, it's their biggest single yet at No. 12.

years.h: Out Spaced comes in a rubber nipple-shaped sleeve
years.p: The compilation gathers the Ankst EPs, favourite B-sides and newly cleared tracks.

years.h: NME readers vote them best new band, three years after their debut
years.p: The album that followed would be their most experimental yet.

years.src: Wikipedia: Guerrilla · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: Guerrilla, made at Peter Gabriel's Real World
years.p: Samples over brass and percussion, recorded at Real World Studios in Box. It reaches No. 10; Pitchfork gives it 9.5.
years.xp: NME called it "an acid fried quadrophonic vision of rock 'n' roll" and made it No. 3 of the year. "Northern Lites" reached No. 11.

years.cap: Poster for the German dates of the Guerrilla tour, August-September 1999
years.src: Wikipedia: Guerrilla · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: Cardiff International Arena hears the first surround-sound concert
years.p: The last Guerrilla show is also webcast on the band's website. On New Year's Eve they support [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]] at the Millennium Stadium.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mwng · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: A £6,000 Welsh-language album reaches No. 11
years.p: With Alan McGee gone from Creation in January, Mwng comes out on the band's own Placid Casual label, the first Welsh-language record in the Top 20.
years.xp:
It was recorded in 1999 at Ofn in Anglesey, Famous in Cardiff and Real World. Rhys called it "a stand against globalisation."

On June 6, Plaid Cymru MP Elfyn Llwyd tabled Early Day Motion 800 in the House of Commons congratulating the band. It remains the biggest-selling Welsh-language album.

eras.title: Celery from McCartney, no to Coca-Cola
eras.text: Epic gave the band a major-label budget and they spent it on a DVD album nobody had tried before. When that deal ran out, Rough Trade put out the last two records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rings Around the World · Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals
years.h: Paul McCartney chews celery on Rings Around the World
years.p: The first album released on CD and DVD on the same day. [[Paul McCartney|ba550d0e-adac-4864-b88b-407cab5e76af]] supplies the vegetable percussion on "Receptacle for the Respectable," [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] plays piano on "Presidential Suite."
years.xp:
McCartney's celery and carrot echoes his part on a Beach Boys track. The album went to No. 3, went gold and was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize. Mojo made it album of the year; NME called it the band's weakest.

At the Mercury ceremony, held just after 9/11, the band played "It's Not the End of the World?"

years.h: Phantom Power goes to No. 4
years.p: Preceded by "Golden Retriever" at No. 13. A remix version, Phantom Phorce, followed with Four Tet and Killa Kela.

years.h: Coca-Cola offers $1.8 million for "Hello Sunshine." The band says no
years.p: They had been to Colombia with War on Want and heard about killings of trade unionists there, Wikipedia reports.

years.cap: Gruff Rhys, Huw Bunford and Guto Pryce at Bridgwater Palace, September 2005
years.h: On Love Kraft, four Furries write and sing
years.p: Rhys, Bunford, Ieuan and Ciaran all take songs and lead vocals. It's the last record of the Epic deal.

years.h: Hey Venus!, recorded in a French château for Rough Trade
years.p: Rhys called it "speaker blowing." It reaches No. 11 and the iTunes top 10.

years.h: Dark Days/Light Years arrives first on the band's own website
years.p: The physical release follows on Rough Trade. [[Franz Ferdinand|aa7a2827-f74b-473c-bd79-03d065835cf7]]'s Nick McCarthy guests on "Inaugural Trams." It's their ninth album, and to date their last.

eras.title: Hiatus, with the door left open
eras.text: The band stopped in 2010 to let everyone finish other projects, and kept coming back: for a footballer, for a reissue, for Wales at the Euros, and, three decades on, for the songs they made before Creation.

years.cap: Super Furry Animals in São Paulo
years.src: Wikipedia: Super Furry Animals · Wikipedia: Gruff Rhys
years.h: Super Furry Animals pause for side projects
years.p: Pryce said they expected to reconvene once everyone finished what they were working on. Rhys's solo records and [[Neon Neon|6191360a-edc5-41d7-a83e-c9f0ab842f53]] filled the time.

years.h: One show at Cardiff City Stadium for Gary Speed
years.p: The band reunites before Wales v Costa Rica, the memorial match for the late Wales manager.

years.cap: Super Furry Animals at Cardiff University's Great Hall, May 2015
years.h: Back on stage, and Mwng back in print
years.p: Reunion gigs line up with a reissue of the out-of-print Welsh-language album. HarperCollins publishes Rise of the Super Furry Animals.

years.cap: Super Furry Animals at Rock City, Nottingham, 2016
years.h: "Bing Bong" celebrates Wales at Euro 2016
years.p: Their first single in seven years. In December they play Fuzzy Logic and Radiator in full around the UK and Ireland.

years.h: Four Furries, no Gruff, become Das Koolies
years.p: Bunford, Ciaran, Pryce and Ieuan revive an electronic alter ego from around 2000. "It's All About The Dolphins" follows in January 2020.

years.h: The 1993 demo with Rhys Ifans surfaces for one week
years.p: "Of No Fixed Identity," the band's first recording, goes up on Bandcamp for a week, with proceeds to the Save the Severn campaign.

years.h: A May 2026 tour, and the Ankst years on one record
years.p: The band announces dates for May 2026. Precreation Percolation, the two Ankst EPs plus Ifans-era demos, is set for May 1, 2026.
